title: Nonlocal Magic across the Many-Body Localization Crossover
abstract: Nonlocal magic quantifies the minimum nonstabilizerness attainable under independent local unitary transformations on the two subsystems. Here, we use min-relative nonlocal magic (NLM) to characterize the crossover from ergodicity to many-body localization (MBL) in the random-field XXZ chain. Unlike entanglement entropy, NLM probes how entanglement is organized through the distance of the Schmidt spectrum from dyadic-flat stabilizer spectra. From weak to intermediate disorder, NLM evolves from an $O(1)$ Haar-like value into a size-enhanced dome, while entanglement remains volume-law, revealing a spectral reorganization not visible in the entropy. Deep in the MBL regime, a two-level cut-hybridization model captures the nearly binary Schmidt spectrum and explains why the mean and median NLM decay approximately as $W^{-1}$ and $W^{-2}$, respectively. Following a product-state quench, NLM overshoots and relaxes in the ergodic regime, whereas at strong disorder it grows slowly and approximately logarithmically. These results show that NLM resolves Schmidt-spectrum structure not visible in the entanglement entropy and provides a complementary probe of ergodicity breaking.
summary: The authors introduce Min-relative Nonlocal Magic ($	ext{DNL}_{\min}$) as a novel diagnostic tool to characterize the transition from ergodic to Many-Body Localization (MBL) in disordered quantum chains. They show that $	ext{DNL}_{\min}$ captures structural information about entanglement, revealing distinct scaling behaviors in the MBL regime that are missed by standard entanglement entropy. This provides a deeper understanding of ergodicity breaking in complex quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop diagnostics beyond entanglement entropy to characterize the crossover from ergodic to Many-Body Localization (MBL) in interacting quantum systems.
main_result: The proposed measure, Min-relative Nonlocal Magic (NLM), reveals a spectral reorganization in the Schmidt spectrum that is invisible to entanglement entropy, showing distinct scaling behaviors in the ergodic and MBL regimes.
method: The analysis involves calculating the minimum-relative NLM ($	ext{DNL}_{\min}$) for a disordered XXZ chain and comparing its scaling properties across different disorder strengths ($W$) and system sizes ($L$).
model_or_system: The primary system is the random-field XXZ chain, $H = J \sum (\dots) + \sum h_i S^z_i$, studied in the half-filling sector. The analysis also utilizes a minimal two-configuration cut-hybridization model to derive analytical scaling laws.
key_observables: Min-relative Nonlocal Magic ($	ext{DNL}_{\min}$), Von Neumann entropy ($S_A$), and state-resolved probability distributions $	ext{P}_X(x)$.
important_parameters: Disorder Strength ($W$), System Size ($L$), and the crossover between ergodic and MBL regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing the behavior of $	ext{DNL}_{\min}$ to established scaling laws for entanglement entropy and utilizes effective low-energy models (e.g., two-level Hamiltonian) to explain decay rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of $	ext{DNL}_{\min}$ and $S_A$ versus disorder strength $W$, showing the dome formation for $	ext{DNL}_{\min}$ versus the volume-to-area law transition for $S_A$. Other figures detail quench dynamics and state-resolved probability distributions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces $	ext{DNL}_{\min}$ as a diagnostic tool, analyzes its behavior across the disorder landscape (weak $	o$ intermediate $	o$ strong), derives scaling laws in the deep MBL regime using minimal models, and finally examines quench dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, quantitative tool ($	ext{DNL}_{\min}$) to probe the underlying structure of entanglement (Schmidt spectrum) in strongly correlated and disordered systems, offering complementary insights to standard entropy measures relevant to open quantum systems dynamics.
